💡 Key Takeaways
  • Restrictions were made after a driverless Waymo was caught trying to pass a Highway Patrol vehicle that was slowing traffic.
  • According to recent reports, california's Department of Motor Vehicles has barred Waymo from operating its robotaxis on state freeways, saying in a statement to Engadget that the firm's driverless operation poses an "imminent hazard to public safety." The restriction has been in place since November 11, according to the DMV.
  • The DMV cited an incident of three Waymo robotaxis entering a restricted construction zone near Burlingame, and a separate incident of a Waymo trying to pass a California Highway Patrol car that was slowing traffic as part of its justification.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Restrictions were made after a driverless Waymo was caught trying to pass a Highway Patrol vehicle that was slowing traffic.

According to recent reports, california's Department of Motor Vehicles has barred Waymo from operating its robotaxis on state freeways, saying in a statement to Engadget that the firm's driverless operation poses an "imminent hazard to public safety." The restriction has been in place since November 11, according to the DMV. In response, Waymo indicates it has temporarily restricted freeway driving in all of its US markets.

The DMV cited an incident of three Waymo robotaxis entering a restricted construction zone near Burlingame, and a separate incident of a Waymo trying to pass a California Highway Patrol car that was slowing traffic as part of its justification. Past examples of Waymo robotaxis attempting to drive through freeway construction sites were part of the reason Waymo voluntarily paused freeway service in May and later recalled 3,800 vehicles in June. The organization started letting its vehicles drive on highways again in July, but whatever fixes were introduced apparently didn't fully address the problem.

"Safety is at the foundation of everything we do," Waymo mentioned in a statement to Engadget. "Following recent freeway construction zone encounters on U.S. 101 in California that did not involve any injuries or collisions, the California DMV has implemented an operating restriction on freeway operations in the state. In alignment with our safety-first principles, we have also temporarily restricted freeway operations across our other operating markets to evaluate our performance.".

In a state like California, losing access to the freeway could significantly change the routes robotaxis are able to take, the length of rides and the cost of using Waymo over a service like Lyft or Uber. Waymo will have to prove to the DMV that it has "taken effective corrective actions to address the deficiencies that precipitated the restrictions" before the freeway ban is lifted.

Recent findings suggest that the company says it will continue offering service on surface streets while it works with regulators. It may also test freeway driving in vehicles with human safety drivers outside of California. Waymo began running robotaxis on California freeways in November 2025, and expanded its service area across Sacramento, the Bay Area and San Diego in August 2026.

Latest Update: Amazon and Google will together own nearly 30% of Anthropic after its IPO

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (451 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: TechCrunch

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Anthropic on Tuesday disclosed more details about the biggest investment agreements with major cloud providers Amazon and Google.
  • While we already knew that Amazon stood to make a killing on its Anthropic investments from the IPO, Anthropic revealed that Amazon’s total stake will come in at just shy of 15% (14.7% to be exact).
  • Sources indicate that even more interesting is that Amazon could have, if it wished, owned an even bigger share of the firm.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anthropic on Tuesday disclosed more details about the biggest investment agreements with major cloud providers Amazon and Google.

While we already knew that Amazon stood to make a killing on its Anthropic investments from the IPO, Anthropic revealed that Amazon’s total stake will come in at just shy of 15% (14.7% to be exact).

Sources indicate that even more interesting is that Amazon could have, if it wished, owned an even bigger share of the firm. When Amazon invested billions in Anthropic in 2023 and 2024 (long before Claude Code took the enterprise world by storm, back in the days when Anthropic looked like it would forever be a speck in OpenAI’s shadow), the cloud giant obtained promissory notes that could convert into equity.

These notes carry conversion prices of about $2.09 or $5.05 per share, depending on the year of investment. Amazon has opted to convert a chunk of them as part of the IPO into a special class of non-voting shares that will give it about 15% ownership. (The shares can receive dividends and convert to standard voting Class A shares when sold, the filing notes).

But it has also opted to hold on to billions of dollars’ worth of the notes for now. If it converted them all right now, it would own just under 24% of Anthropic (23.8% to be precise).

Sources indicate that google, meanwhile, will own just under 14% (13.7%), also in non-voting shares, which come from the conversion of notes, as well as the “private placement” sale of shares as part of this IPO. A group of major tech companies (AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia, and TSMC Partners) have agreed to buy $26 billion worth of this non-voting stock. Google and Nvidia each agreed to buy $10 billion worth.

So while a lot of investors stand to make billions of dollars in Anthropic’s IPO, Amazon is one of the biggest winners, and that doesn’t even count that AWS stands to earn from Anthropic’s commitment to spend more than $100 billion on its cloud services over the next decade.

“Trump was in bed with Jensen”: Critics balk at Huang’s wish to return to Nvidia

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1976 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • On Monday, large trucks began circling the streets of Washington, DC, carrying billboards urging Congress to investigate the Trump administration’s ties with Nvidia’s disgraced CEO Jensen Huang.
  • According to recent reports, “Jensen was in bed with a spy from China,” the billboards created by the Tech Oversight Project (TOP) alleged.
  • Presently, Trump is supporting a campaign to bring back Huang as Nvidia’s CEO—despite many Republicans calling it a “horrible idea.” Breaking his silence, Huang issued a statement Tuesday saying he would be “honored” to return, but the board remarked reinstatement is not under consideration as an internal investigation into US spying claims remains ongoing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On Monday, large trucks began circling the streets of Washington, DC, carrying billboards urging Congress to investigate the Trump administration’s ties with Nvidia’s disgraced CEO Jensen Huang.

According to recent reports, “Jensen was in bed with a spy from China,” the billboards created by the Tech Oversight Project (TOP) alleged. “Trump was in bed with Jensen.” TOP is a nonprofit that describes itself as “dedicated to reining in Significant Tech.”.

Presently, Trump is supporting a campaign to bring back Huang as Nvidia’s CEO—despite many Republicans calling it a “horrible idea.” Breaking his silence, Huang issued a statement Tuesday saying he would be “honored” to return, but the board remarked reinstatement is not under consideration as an internal investigation into US spying claims remains ongoing. Huang used the moment to say that his interests align with the US’s, saying:.

I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. Nvidia has been my life’s work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor. Nowhere but in America could a company like Nvidia be possible. I love our country, and I love Nvidia.

Trump may have learned as early as this spring that Huang was potentially the target of Chinese espionage, but the president claimed recently that he didn’t know Huang was potentially exposed to a Chinese spy as he was becoming a prominent part of Trump’s inner circle, CNN reported.

If Trump wasn’t adequately briefed, it raises question about whether the White House acted with “sufficient urgency” to address a serious espionage threat, CNN remarked. But if Trump is deflecting, an even “graver question” will emerge about why Trump didn’t act on information and instead continued to keep Huang close, CNN said.

Instead of distancing himself from the Nvidia CEO, Trump invited Huang to sit at the head table during a state dinner with China’s president Xi Jinping, and last month, Trump awarded Huang the National Medal of Science, the nation’s highest scientiﬁc honor, for his AI achievements.

“Not only has he continued to do nothing, he’s invited that very CEO into the White House and on state visits to China with him,” Sacha Haworth, TOP’s founder and CEO, told Ars. “And the question we all have to ask is ‘why on Earth would he do that?’”.

Sources indicate that what Trump and Nvidia knew—and when—have become central questions for some Republicans, as well as top Democrats who strategy to investigate the scandal when they assume control of key committees in Congress next year. Andrew Yoon, head of research for a nonprofit called CivAI, which warns the public of dangers from AI, told Ars that Huang doesn’t need to be compromised by China to have endangered the US. Prioritizing boosting profits over national security alone is “pretty concerning.”.

Sources indicate that “I think the most notable thing here is that Jensen Huang has been at the absolute forefront of lobbying to be able to sell chips to China,” Yoon stated. “He has leveraged his very deep relationships with government, especially President Trump, in order to be able to sell as many Nvidia chips to China as he can get away with. If he could be selling Blackwell chips to China, I’m sure he would be.”.

Yoon noted that evidence suggests some Chinese AI models have been trained on Blackwell chips. Even with China’s push to prioritize domestic chipmakers like Huawei, Nvidia chips remain “indispensable” to China’s frontier AI goals, Yoon said. And national security experts fear that access to high-end chips will help China advance its military AI or gain economic ground.

Sources indicate that the White House isn’t commenting on Trump’s relationship with Huang. Among the lawmakers accusing the Trump administration of “corruption” is Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), The Wall Street Journal reported. He has already asked the White House to “preserve all communications” between Trump and Huang.

Other lawmakers are “seeking more information about what Trump knew about the relationship between Jensen Huang and Alice Huang,” the former Megaspeed CEO whom Huang admitted to having an affair with. They also want to know more about “the administration’s failure to stop artiﬁcial-intelligence chips from going to China,” WSJ reported, and Nvidia’s reportedly $25 million donation to the White House ballroom.

“It is not just an intelligence issue; it’s also a potential corruption issue,” Blumenthal noted. “There needs to be a really penetrating, comprehensive investigation of all the possible compromises of our intelligence that may have occurred, but also… that Donald Trump is so high on the head of Nvidia, and now is potentially linked to intelligence compromises.”.

Sources indicate that trump has profited off Nvidia’s success while in office, buying “millions of dollars worth of Nvidia shares in his personal brokerage accounts since returning to oﬃce in 2025,” the WSJ reported. The White House maintains that the president has no role in managing his stock portfolio.

Other officials advising Trump on AI also benefited from relaxing export curbs, TOP said. On Tuesday, the group issued a report summarizing what the public knows about potential conflicts of interest of two Trump officials: former White House AI Czar David Sacks and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick.

Haworth, TOP’s founder, told Ars she’s concerned that Sacks and Lutnick abused their power to convince Trump to let Nvidia sell cutting-edge technology to China, while standing to “gain astronomical amounts of money.”.

Sources indicate that “The public is outraged by Nvidia’s CEO for compromising our national security, but we didn’t get here because of Jensen Huang’s missteps alone,” Haworth noted. If “Nvidia was knowingly doing business with companies tied to illegal chip sales and smuggling with China,” then “the Trump administration was asleep at the wheel,” she said.

“White House AI Czar David Sacks and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick were protecting their own fortunes rather than looking out for Americans,” Haworth said.

If the US fails to hold them accountable for alleged conflicts of interest, “it would send a signal that powerful men once again cannot be held to account and that powerful men are protecting powerful men,” Haworth remarked.

According to recent reports, detailing Sacks’ alleged conflicts, the group cited Fresh York Times reporting that the former AI czar had long supported Huang’s stance that allowing Nvidia to sell more chips in China would help the US stay ahead in the AI race. After Sacks became Trump’s key AI advisor, Huang rapidly forged a “tight bond” with him, and “both stood to benefit” from their push to sell chips to China, TOP reported.

In a recent development, also notably, while advising the White House, Sacks opposed policies such as the Trump administration’s recent move to cut off China’s remote access to US-made chips through now-restricted Southeast Asian data centers. Citing Sacks’ alignment with Huang, TOP reported that after just one meeting with the two men, Trump decided to allow Nvidia to sell AI chips to China that the Biden administration had previously blocked.

Industry observers note that huang valued his alliance with Sacks, TOP noted, citing reporting that showed Huang declaring last year that Nvidia was “lucky” to have Sacks advising Trump. But TOP is concerned that the alliance was built on mutual financial interest and that Sacks took a part-time role in the Trump administration to avoid divestments or disclosure requirements that might have revealed the extent of his possible conflicts of interest.

Recent findings suggest that TOP flagged two areas it believes warrant Congressional investigation. While advising Trump to embrace AI deregulation, Sacks and his firm, Craft Ventures, continued investing substantially in AI. Sacks also stood to benefit from pushing Trump to integrate AI into warfare and national security tools, TOP’s report said. Craft Ventures has invested in Palantir, “a Peter Thiel-founded government contractor seen as a ‘rising star’ in the US Defense Tech World and holding hundreds of millions in US government defense contracts,” TOP said.

Even within the Trump administration, officials have turned on Commerce Secretary Lutnick, seemingly looking to blame him for mishandling the Nvidia spying investigation and allowing Trump to maintain close ties with Huang despite apparent intelligence risks.

Recent findings suggest that lutnick has bragged publicly that he promised Huang “really easy access to the President” after joining the administration, TOP reported. That alliance helped push Trump to approve the sale of Nvidia H200s to China, TOP stated. And that seemed to directly benefit Lutnick, TOP said, because before he was confirmed as secretary, he was CEO of Cantor Fitzgerald, which held $1.2 billion in Nvidia stock.

It has been revealed that “In his role as Secretary, Lutnick is responsible for policing exports of sensitive technology to adversaries and global rivals, like China,” TOP reported. “Lutnick and the organization he controls benefited greatly from opening sales of Nvidia chips to China.”.

After Lutnick was required to hand that tech giant over to his son, Cantor Fitzgerald “maintained extensive commercial ties to Nvidia, helping arrange billions of dollars in financing for companies in its AI business universe and repeatedly hosting its top executives,” TOP noted.

Sources indicate that those investments shifted substantially around the same time that Lutnick began facing pressure to “crack down on Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company suspected of funneling Nvidia’s advanced artificial intelligence chips to China,” TOP reported. Cantor Fitzgerald “reduced its Nvidia holdings by nearly 50 percent between September 2025 and March 2026,” TOP said.

However, when Trump was reportedly first told of the spying allegations this spring, Cantor Fitzgerald again continued to boost Nvidia. Most prominently, the company helped “finance the expansion of one of Nvidia’s newest business partners, IREN,” facilitating a five-year, $3.4 billion deal between Nvidia and the Australia-based cloud computing provider.

Among those now criticizing Lutnick for weak enforcement of export controls that appeared designed to protect Huang’s bottom line is Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. But even with scrutiny coming from within the Trump administration, not everyone is convinced that Lutnick did anything wrong. Yoon suggested that, given Lutnick’s long career, there may be normal explanations for potential financial conflicts.

“Maybe a separate question is ‘should people with a long storied history in business and industry be working in government at this level?’” Yoon remarked.

Haworth remarked the next 48 hours will be critical in determining whether Huang succeeds in returning to Nvidia.

“I think it’s going to be incumbent on the incoming Democratic leadership to insist that whether or not he returns, investigations will follow,” Haworth said.

But Yoon thinks Nvidia is unlikely to bring Huang back any time soon, despite current evidence suggesting that “Nvidia’s actions here have been perfectly legal” and that “influencing a political system for your financial interests is very much legal in the United States.”.

Industry observers note that it seems “untenable for Nvidia to continue doing what they’re doing,” Yoon noted. Zooming out even more, he suggested the scandal demonstrated that the entire AI industry can no longer afford to operate under a profit motive alone, so long as governments continue positioning the technology as a strategic asset.

In a recent development, if US investigations expose corruption, bribery, treason, or other crimes, Nvidia risks losing some of its dominant stake in the GPU market. On Tuesday, The Information reported that some Nvidia customers had already lost trust and were looking to Google and AMD for more stability.

Nvidia has also been accused of intervening in a Commerce investigation, which Yoon said could also be “pretty consequential” if any evidence bears that out.

In a recent development, “I think it’s pretty unlikely that Huang makes it back to Nvidia any time soon,” Yoon said. “Maybe he goes on a redemption tour and comes back in five years or something, but I’m not really seeing a path forward for him right now.”.

Autonomous cab giant Waymo has suspended freeway access for its fleet of vehicles following a safety notice from the California Department of Motor Vehicles.

Frist reported by the San Francisco Business Times, the California DMV issued a notice on Nov. 11 that a small number of Waymo vehicles in the San Francisco Bay Area had entered restricted construction zones on U.S. Route 101 despite notice of closures. Another vehicle reportedly impeded California Highway Patrol on Highway 280.

Because of these "recurring incursions," the state revealed it would ban self-driving taxis from state freeways until the company implemented "effective corrective actions," the DMV said in a statement to TechCrunch. The department called the incidents an imminent hazard to public safety.

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

Waymo, which is owned by Google's parent holding manufacturer, Alphabet, responded by pausing freeway access for its entire nationwide fleet. Freeways had been accessible to Waymo cabs in select cities since 2025, with a brief, unexplained pause from May to July of this year.

Recent findings suggest that "In alignment with our safety-first principles, we have also temporarily restricted freeway operations across our other operating markets to evaluate our performance," said Waymo spokesperson Dana Gallagher. "Our ride-hailing service continues to operate safely on surface streets, serving over half a million trips each week. We are working with the California DMV and other state officials diligently and responsibly to resume freeway operations.".

According to recent reports, several viral incidents of Waymo cabs driving erratically, ignoring obstacles, and being easily impeded by human obstructions have stoked concern about the nationwide rollout of autonomous vehicles. Video footage of the California Highway Patrol incident demonstrates a Waymo driving toward two CHP vehicles leading a traffic break. The Waymo attempts to go around the vehicles despite the flashing lights and officers' weaving.

The manufacturer recently announced an expansion into Denver, San Diego, and Tampa markets, as well as a new collaboration with San Francisco Bay Area transit agencies.

  • At the time, the feature wasn’t available even to beta testers, but WABetaInfo’s report provided details on how it would work, including 2GB of free storage, optional paid aims for larger backups, and mandatory end-to-end encryption for backups stored on WhatsApp’s servers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, select WhatsApp beta testers on iOS are now seeing an option to use the app’s own backup service as an alternative to iCloud. Here are the details.

A few months ago, WABetaInfo reported that WhatsApp was working on its own backup service as an alternative to the current method of backing up chats, which relies on Apple’s iCloud.

At the time, the feature wasn’t available even to beta testers, but WABetaInfo’s report provided details on how it would work, including 2GB of free storage, optional paid aims for larger backups, and mandatory end-to-end encryption for backups stored on WhatsApp’s servers.

Now, the site reports that some WhatsApp users running the latest TestFlight build are seeing the option to switch from iCloud to WhatsApp’s own backup service, suggesting that a wider rollout may not be too far off.

It has been revealed that consumers can switch to WhatsApp cloud storage from the Chat backup screen. Here, users will have to choose the backup provider they want to use. If they choose WhatsApp, they will have to secure their backups using end-to-end encryption. Since encryption is mandatory, users cannot skip this step. However, they can choose a different method to encrypt their backups. For example, users can secure their backups using a 64-digit encryption key. Users who do not know what to choose can opt for the passkey, which is the default method WhatsApp recommends. After users complete the setup, they can back up their chat history on WhatsApp’s servers. WhatsApp keeps the backup on its servers for four months after a subscription expires. If users do not renew their subscription, WhatsApp deletes the backup permanently.

Importantly, the site notes that backups stored on WhatsApp’s servers cannot currently be used to restore chats across platforms, meaning consumers switching from iPhone to Android, or vice versa, will still need to rely on WhatsApp’s built-in chat transfer feature.

Although the feature appears to be rolling out to beta testers first, the report notes that “the latest version available on the App Store is also compatible with this functionality,” meaning WhatsApp could theoretically enable it for users running the public version without requiring another app upgrade.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple’s inroads on designing repairable devices seems to have been abandoned with the HomeView.﻿.

Apple’s inroads on designing repairable devices seems to have been abandoned with the HomeView.﻿.

According to recent reports, after finding recent versions of Apple’s iPads and HomePods much easier to disassemble for battery replacements or other repairs, iFixit assumed it would be the same story for Apple’s newly introduced HomeView hub that looks like a seven-inch tablet stuck to a smart speaker. The reality was much different and by the time they got the HomeView apart iFixit’s skilled techs had “ripped a connector, snapped a speaker in two, and put more force on the poor logic board than any of us were comfortable with.”.

The tablet section of the HomeView proved to be the bigger challenge to disassemble as a result of some questionable decisions with Apple’s design. The glue used to secure the display in place “held on harder than on any Apple product we’ve opened recently,” iFixit notes. And while Apple’s decision to turn the HomeView’s entire aluminum chassis into a heat sink was clever, the thermal bond between a heat shield and the device’s logic board made separating the two a “remarkably risky operation.” While these design decisions possibly streamlined assembly at a factory, the extensive use of glue makes servicing the HomeView incredibly difficult.

In an accompanying teardown video iFixit also reveals how much smaller the speaker drivers are in the wall-mounted version of the HomeView versus the tabletop option. Although both versions are priced at $299, the wall version costs a little more when you factor in the required mount that’s not included, leaving iFixit feeling that you’re getting less performance while spending more money.

FAA pauses installation of upcoming routers after ground stop

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Federal Aviation Administration said Tuesday it would pause the installation of new routers after problems with the technology led the agency to matter a rare nationwide ground stop on Friday.
  • Tens of thousands of flights were affected by the ground stop, which halted departing flights for more than four hours.
  • Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy noted Sunday that an overloaded router installed in southern Arkansas as part of an upgrade to a system overseen by L3Harris Technologies appeared to overwhelm systems that feed radar and other data for air traffic control.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Federal Aviation Administration said Tuesday it would pause the installation of new routers after problems with the technology led the agency to matter a rare nationwide ground stop on Friday.

Tens of thousands of flights were affected by the ground stop, which halted departing flights for more than four hours. It was the longest halt to U.S. flight departures since 9/11.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy noted Sunday that an overloaded router installed in southern Arkansas as part of an upgrade to a system overseen by L3Harris Technologies appeared to overwhelm systems that feed radar and other data for air traffic control.

The Wall Street Journal first reported the news about the pause.

The FAA and Department of Transportation have stated L3Harris was working to convert the communications network from copper wires to fiber optic.

Democratic members of the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science and Transportation this week asked the FAA and the Department of Transportation for clarity on what went wrong.

In a recent development, "Identifying the device that failed does not establish why it failed," the senators wrote in a statement. "Modernization cannot come at the expense of operational safety.".

The agencies have said they are working to figure out the root cause of the issue and have reiterated that there is no indication of a cyberattack or outside threat.

The senators also asked for a briefing with the FAA, L3Harris and Juniper Networks, which is making the new devices, by Monday. They asked the companies to lay out why the operational systems lacked sufficient redundancy and answer other questions about what led to the outage.

CNBC has reached out to L3Harris and Juniper Networks for comment.

Duffy on Friday called for Congress to approve $50 billion in funding for upgrades to the aging U.S. air traffic control system, more than he has previously asked for. Democratic lawmakers pushed back on the request, citing unspent money from existing funding, which includes Congress' approval last year of $12.5 billion for airport and air traffic control improvements over five years.

Senate Commerce Chair Ted Cruz, R-Texas, said Tuesday that he thinks there will be support for air traffic control modernization, but that the allocation should be specifically for safety upgrades.

"I don't think the full $50 billion will be funded," he said. "Some of that is not safety related, but we just discussed there, and what I expressed is that the request needs to be focused on safety modernization.".

In a recent development, duffy dismissed the idea that the router glitch had to do with the introduction of artificial intelligence tools and mentioned it was "completely unfounded" because the AI system is not in communication with the defective router. He added that the FBI is helping to investigate the root cause of the issue.

Aging equipment and a shortage of air traffic controllers have for years angered airline executives, who have complained about the cost of resulting disruptions.

— CNBC's Phil LeBeau, Leslie Josephs and Justin Papp contributed to this report.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Otherwise, NVIDIA had a great Q3.

Recent findings suggest that harvey Jones, NVIDIA's recently appointed board chair, joined the manufacturer's Q3 earnings call on Tuesday to comment on the resignation of Jensen Huang. Despite the former CEO floating the possibility of a potential return to his old position, Harvey quashed the possibility, saying the board was not considering reinstating Huang. Jones later said he and Colette Kress, the company's upcoming interim CEO, would not answer any questions related to Huang.

According to recent reports, "On November 12th, our board of directors announced that after disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company's code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms, Jensen Huang voluntarily resigned his positions as president, CEO, and board member," Jones mentioned. "The NVIDIA board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.".

During the call, Kress stated that the tech giant was prioritizing its employees. "We will take care of our employees during this transition to make sure that they are safe and making sure the work can be done in the current environment," she said. And while she didn't mention Huang or his resignation directly, she said that "there's also a time to think about our leadership and how important our leadership is across this organization." Mostly though, she tried to keep the call focused on NVIDIA's blockbuster quarter, saying that "from [a] business perspective, it's business as usual," for the chip giant.

The statements came alongside NVIDIA's first earnings report since Huang resigned. The organization easily beat investor expectations for the quarter. On Tuesday, NVIDIA remarked revenue increased to $115.8 billion for the three-month period ending October 25. The new number represents a 103 percent increase year-over-year from Q3 2025, and a 20 percent increase from its most recent previous quarter. Going into Tuesday, Wall Street analysts expected the company's revenue to land somewhere in the range of $109.1 billion.The company's data center revenue, which accounts for the majority of its earnings, more than doubled to $107.6 billion. Here again, the company easily beat expectations.

In a recent development, we're likely to learn in the next day or two whether today's earnings numbers are enough to calm investors. Huang was still NVIDIA's CEO for the entirety of the tech giant's third quarter, with Kress only holding the position for all of the past four business days. Since Huang's resignation on November 12, NVIDIA's stock had fallen about 11 percent.

Ahead of Tuesday's earnings, Huang stated he was willing to return to the company. "If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO," he wrote in a statement shared on X. Given the timing of the post, Huang's statement could be read as an attempt to pressure NVIDIA's board to give him his position back.

During the call, Jones remarked the manufacturer's board of directors is taking the search for a upcoming CEO "very seriously" and was considering internal and external candidates. "The board appreciates that we're living in a world where the advanced silicon technologies and national security dynamics are making major changes in our marketplace," he said. "Our new CEO will have to navigate those those waters very carefully, so the the the search will be thorough, and we want to install the CEO, the permanent CEO, as rapidly as possible. But we won't expedite the CEO before finding exactly the right person.".

In addition to the search for a new leader, NVIDIA will have its hands full dealing with fallout from recent revelations. According to a report The Wall Street Journal published before market close, the US Securities and Exchange Commission recently began investigating NVIDIA. The outlet said it could not immediately learn the focus of the probe. The FBI is also looking into the matter, according to President Donald Trump.

If Kress is rattled by any of this, it wasn't immediately apparent in her remarks to analysts. "Our momentum is real," she mentioned at the end of the call. "Our demand is accelerating. Our supply is growing. Our customers and our partners are with us, and employees are committed. We've got this.".

Hundreds of websites deliver potent malware cocktail to unsuspecting visitors

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (564 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Optimizely serves JavaScript “snippets” that include both manufacturer code and code that is provided by each customer.
  • ReportURI researcher Scott Helme noted the delivery mechanism wasn’t a CDN cache poisoning attack, which uses HTTP to cause a CDN to cache harmful responses.
  • It has been revealed that “We don’t know how the attacker got write access to so many unrelated customer projects: a compromised Optimizely system, a compromised credential with cross-customer access, or something else,” ReportURI Helme wrote.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Optimizely serves JavaScript “snippets” that include both manufacturer code and code that is provided by each customer. The JavaScript, which can be served directly from Optimizely or from a customer endpoint, runs on every page the customer serves. Somehow, the attackers wrote their own code into a portion of each affected customer’s JavaScript and then delivered it from cdn.optimizely.com. A valid certificate for that domain signed the JavaScript.

ReportURI researcher Scott Helme noted the delivery mechanism wasn’t a CDN cache poisoning attack, which uses HTTP to cause a CDN to cache harmful responses. Instead, the attack relied on Optimizely’s legitimate infrastructure, including its domains, to serve the tainted code. Optimizely’s own customer JavaScript for the www.optimizely.com and login.optimizely.com URLs were also affected.

It has been revealed that “We don’t know how the attacker got write access to so many unrelated customer projects: a compromised Optimizely system, a compromised credential with cross-customer access, or something else,” ReportURI Helme wrote. “That’s for Optimizely to explain.”.

Optimizely representatives didn’t respond to questions sent by email.

The scripts were named track.js, and all four components became active at the same time. Devices that received the malicious code responded differently depending on their platform and what they were doing on the final page delivering it. Actions performed included:.

In a recent development, 1. Crypto wallet address swapping. The script searches for wallet addresses for nine different cryptocurrencies and, when found, replaces them with one of the attacker’s. ReportURI said funds have already been stolen from some people whose devices ran the code.

In a recent development, 2. Card skimming. The script watches HTTP requests for payment card numbers, expiry dates, and CVVs. When all three are present, it sends them to https://1688360.cc/card.php. Cards entered in hosted payment iframes such as Stripe and Adyen were unaffected.

4. The DarkSword and Coruna exploit kits for iOS. The kits are delivered through a file named boot.js served from 5vobauua3ojpklx.icu and eil786npto9u5bq.icu. The file delivers a hidden iframe that contains an exploit chain tailored to the iOS version being used. Coruna can infect iOS versions 13 to 17. DarkSword can infect versions 18.x. A separate chain for iOS 26 fingerprints devices but doesn’t appear to do anything else. Earlier this month, researchers saw hackers possibly linked to the Kremlin attempting to deliver DarkSword through multiple vectors, including a compromised web analytics service.

Industry observers note that the list of sites that ReportURI found delivering the malicious scripts numbers 178, and as noted, includes many big names. It’s unclear if the list is exhaustive. Helme said in an interview that “Ars wasn’t affected as far as we saw, and I haven’t seen any other indications it was.” Website administrators can check both the ReportURI post and this one from security firm Cynet for indicators of compromise.

At the moment, there’s no information available on how successful the exploit chains were in installing the payloads. Beyond the bare-bones details above, more precise information about what versions of iOS were susceptible was also unavailable. These sorts of gaps are common in breaking news concerning mass malware attacks, because it takes time for researchers to sift through the evidence. Readers are encouraged to check back as new developments come to light.

The indicators may help end owners determine if they are affected, but the skill required is likely out of reach for many.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Following last week’s launch of the Apple HomeView, iFixit today published its teardown of the device.
  • Contrary to recent teardowns, which found significant repairability improvements with greater component modularity and easier access to internal components, the HomeView put up a fight nearly all the way through.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that iFixit’s teardown of the latest Apple HomeView is now up, revealing a device that seems nearly impossible to take apart and repair. Watch it below.

Following last week’s launch of the Apple HomeView, iFixit today published its teardown of the device.

Contrary to recent teardowns, which found significant repairability improvements with greater component modularity and easier access to internal components, the HomeView put up a fight nearly all the way through.

With heavily glued or adhesive-bonded components, including the display, speakers, antennas, and logic board, the teardown proved particularly challenging, even after the adhesive securing the display’s speakers was soaked in isopropyl alcohol.

At one point, one of them broke apart during removal, while the logic board required considerable force to separate from the chassis due to the thermal adhesive holding it in place.

Industry observers note that iFixit’s teardown covered the two HomeView variants: the tabletop model and the wall-mounted version. Interestingly, there are some internal differences between them, as the wall-mounted model has a slightly wider logic board to accommodate capacitors that are housed in the base of the tabletop version.

As a result, the wall-mounted HomeView also has smaller internal speakers, which helps explain the differences in their audio systems that Apple had already acknowledged at launch.

Back to the tabletop model, iFixit’s teardown also highlighted that separating the display from the base requires either specialized tools or extensive, potentially destructive disassembly of the display assembly, thanks to the way Apple routed the connecting cables through the pivot mechanism.

Once iFixit was in the base, however, there was some good news: the USB-C port is modular and relatively easy to access, as are the passive radiators and the board powering the lower assembly.

Still, an extremely short cable connecting the woofer to the board underneath made disassembly difficult, with iFixit questioning how anyone would be able to reconnect it during reassembly.

Given all these repairability challenges, Shahram Mokhtari joked that while iFixit doesn’t have an official repairability scorecard for this category of device, he would give the Apple HomeView a “BEEP this thing” out of 10.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Following a change in how it counts views earlier this year, YouTube is now announcing “Co-Views” as a way for the platform to try and guess how many people are watching a YouTube video on a TV, and it counts towards the video’s total view count.
  • It has been revealed that view counts on YouTube are still settling from the change earlier this year where YouTube now counts a view after the very first frame of a video plays.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Following a change in how it counts views earlier this year, YouTube is now announcing “Co-Views” as a way for the platform to try and guess how many people are watching a YouTube video on a TV, and it counts towards the video’s total view count.

It has been revealed that view counts on YouTube are still settling from the change earlier this year where YouTube now counts a view after the very first frame of a video plays. But, even with that, YouTube only counts a single view for each time the video is played.

Now, YouTube indicates it might count more views with a newly introduced “Co-Views” setup on TVs.

In a post, YouTube explains that “Co-Views” include “the estimated number of people watching together on TV” in the view count of a video. This only applies to TVs, with views from a mobile device or desktop still only ever counting as a single video. It applies to long-form videos as well as Shorts and Live videos, and only applies going forward – historical data won’t change.

YouTube says it is making this change to reflect the “over 1 billion hours” spend on YouTube through their TVs “every day” and that the added data will assist creators in channel strategy or brand pitches, while also providing a “more complete picture of how audiences are engaging with’ content, aligning with TV industry standards – including how traditional broadcast and streaming networks estimate the total number of people exposed to content.” But “Co-Views” won’t count towards earnings on the platform, as they’re not “Qualified Views.”.

Industry observers note that how is YouTube figuring out what to count here? “Guessing” is not exactly an inaccurate summarization, but Google stresses that it is not using cameras or microphones, but rather a “statistical mode.”.

According to recent reports, youTube doesn’t use devices, cameras, microphones or anything like that. Co-views are estimated using a privacy safe statistical mode, developed by Google research scientists, based on factors like demographic patterns and viewing times, calibrated against ground-truth data sources like industry panels.

This change is rolling out now.

#861. Tech Report: The dangers of using your old, damaged charging cables

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (996 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: The dangers of using your old, damaged charging cables

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (996 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Don't let a damaged $5 cable cost you thousands in fire damage or medical bills.
  • It has been revealed that A charging cable has two key jobs: keep your devices charged, and do so without causing you or the item any damage.
  • In a recent development, if you don't replace a compromised charging cable, you're risking damage to your device or being burnt yourself every time you plug it in.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Don't let a damaged $5 cable cost you thousands in fire damage or medical bills.

It has been revealed that A charging cable has two key jobs: keep your devices charged, and do so without causing you or the item any damage. You can't expect a cable to last forever, though. After being plugged in and disconnected countless times, it's going to degrade, bend, break down, or split apart. The end result is an unsafe cable that will need replacing.

In a recent development, if you don't replace a compromised charging cable, you're risking damage to your device or being burnt yourself every time you plug it in. For the sake of a few dollars, you're better off buying a new one than persevering with a cable that should have been recycled long ago.

Pulling a charging cable out by the wire puts strain on the connection behind the plug. And you're going to bend it sharply in roughly the same places, especially at the two ends. This wears down the fine strands of metal inside before there's any sign of outer damage.

Sources indicate that the funny part is that even if the cable is damaged inside, it can still work, although the connection might keep cutting out. Even if it's to the point where you see a lot of physical damage, it may be able to provide a charge. The remaining strands are carrying the weight, letting the current charge through.

Recent findings suggest that the problem with this is pure physics. With fewer intact strands carrying the current, you're going to see increased electrical resistance. More energy will turn into heat as the current passes through, with that heat concentrated in a smaller area. This is where a damaged cable can start to overheat, especially when it's carrying the higher current used for fast charging.

You might have a charger with safety features designed to protect against overheating or short-circuits, to name but a few. You can't rely on this, though. A damaged connection can still heat up, even if the current passing through your cable is within the safety limits. You might get a warning on your phone about this, if your device has that functionality.

Recent findings suggest that the immediate danger is getting either burned or electrocuted. Heat will concentrate around a damaged connector, making it hot enough to burn your fingers and melt the plastic around it. While the US Consumer Product Safety Commission can recall poorly-made cables, like this heyday Lightning cable sold at Target in 2019, your cable might simply be damaged by overuse. Even with a good cable, charging your device underneath a pillow or blanket isn't a good idea, as this traps the heat.

Sources indicate that potential problems include damaging your device's battery or reducing its long-term health from the inconsistent power going into it. It's also possible for the compromised electrical signals to fry your device's USB port. There's also a risk of electrical shock if you're using a frayed cable. USB leads carry low voltage, but you don't want to chance it. Further shock dangers can occur if the cable is connected to an adapter, or if the adapter itself is exposed. Moisture adds to the risk, too.

The worst-case scenario is a fire. I'm not suggesting every frayed USB cable will lead to a fire, but it's a possibility. A properly functioning charger should have protections against short circuits and excessive current. If the equipment is poorly made, you're not going to have confidence that those protections work. Obviously, the consequences if a fire starts are much bigger than just a broken cable or device.

Sources indicate that you can't expect your home's circuit breaker to protect from this. It responds to faults in the household circuit, but depending on how much current the faulty equipment draws, the breaker might not trip at all. A cable can still become dangerously hot without your electricity cutting out.

Electrical tape (or any sort of tape) is a common solution to wrap around a damaged section of cable. It'll cover the split, but those broken strands inside aren't getting fixed and you shouldn't pretend it's as safe as a new cable. As a temporary fix to charge your device until a replacement arrives tomorrow, it might be fine, but you shouldn't use this for any longer than you have to.

According to recent reports, in most cases, you'll spot when a cable is in bad shape because your device flickers in and out of charging, or it might only charge when you're holding the cable at a particular angle. Propping it up or bending it can provide a quick fix but won't help in the long-term.

Industry observers note that you might also wonder if the problem is with the cable or the port you're plugging it into. There's an easy answer to this: change the cable. If you've got a spare that works perfectly, it's the cable. If it doesn't, it's likely the port. Double-check using a different charger to be sure.

Industry observers note that shine a light inside the port to get a better look. If you see any debris, you might want to give the port a cleaning, although Google advises against putting anything into your phone's port. Lightly tapping your phone against your hand with the port facing down can help dislodge buildup inside.

Sources indicate that you might think this is all somewhat hyperbolic. It's also a bit hypocritical, as I've used fraying charging cables on more than one occasion in a rush (and later regretted it). The cost for a new cable is far less than replacing a broken piece of equipment, covering a medical bill or dealing with fire damage. Unless you're an electrical engineer with the skills to strip and repair a wire and test it afterwards, and have the desire to do so, recycle your old cable or repurpose it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The prediction market platform's CEO has complied but opposed the move.

In a recent development, on November 13, the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission ordered prediction market platform Kalshi to halt mention markets centered on President Donald Trump. The contracts in question were a "TRUMPSAY" series and one titled "What nicknames will Trump say before 2027?" These contract types allowed consumers to bet on whether the president would say particular words in a given time frame.

The CFTC wants to launch "a proceeding to determine whether Kalshi's certification that the contracts comply with the Commodity Exchange Act and the Commission's regulations was false." The prediction market has complied with the order, although Kalshi CEO Tarek Mansour said he is opposed to pausing these bets.

The agency released a staff advisory on these predictions in September, noting that they "present a heightened risk of manipulation because their settlement turns on the discrete conduct of a person that may be neither independently generated nor externally verifiable.".

Mention markets around presidential speeches, as well as predictions markets' possible ties to the current administration, have already stirred controversy. White House teleprompter operator Gabriel Perez was placed on administrative leave this summer after he reportedly made more than $100,000 betting on things that Trump would say. At that time, the CFTC said it would be willing to settle with Perez if he returned the money. Kalshi has also parted ways with Donald Trump Jr as one of its paid advisors; the move was dubbed a mutual decision based on Trump Jr's investment firm putting more funds into rival Polymarket.

It has been revealed that the CFTC has mostly used a light touch in overseeing prediction markets, although the agency has been aggressive in staking its legal claim to be the sole regulator of these businesses. It has sued multiple states that tried to take prediction markets to court on charges that they constitute illegal gambling.

Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress reaffirmed the tech giant’s commitment to open source AI during Tuesday’s earnings call with analysts — the first since CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation.

In a recent development, “At Nvidia, we are committed to fostering a vibrant open model ecosystem, so every country, firm, and industry can build its own intelligence,” Kress said in her opening remarks. She also noted that open models were accelerating AI adoption, citing a 35-fold year-over-year surge in weekly token volume on OpenRouter, including a 3.5-fold increase over the past three months.

Kress also spoke about Nvidia’s plans for Hugging Face, a platform for open source AI models that the company agreed to acquire for $12.9 billion in September, in what would be the second-largest acquisition in Nvidia’s history.

Recent findings suggest that the platform, which serves more than 118 million developers and 200,000 companies, is still on track to join Nvidia, despite Huang’s ouster. Huang had heavily advocated for open source AI technology. His departure had raised questions about the organization’s future approach to open source AI models, with Hugging Face’s CEO calling Huang’s departure “a sad day,” and promising to “keep fighting for open-source AI, harder than ever.”.

So far, Nvidia’s aims for Hugging Face appear unchanged. The acquisition was not directly addressed during the Q&A portion of the earnings call.

“Together, we will scale its platform and make intelligence more open, more capable, and more accessible,” stated Kress of Nvidia’s plans for Hugging Face.

Last week, Nvidia founder Huang resigned from his position as CEO following news about his extramarital affairs, including one with Alice Huang, an executive at the Singapore-based company Megaspeed who is suspected of being a Chinese spy. He’s also accused of having extramarital affairs with two direct reports and is now set to testify before Congress by Thanksgiving. Meanwhile, the SEC is investigating Nvidia over whether the company’s disclosures misled investors, The WSJ reported.

According to recent reports, within Nvidia, Huang pushed for the development of the Nemotron family of open-weight AI models built for long-running agentic AI systems and reasoning workloads. On today’s call, Kress noted that Nemotron is now the “most widely used U.S. open model on OpenRouter,” and it’s “where developers start to build their own intelligence.”.

“That foundation is empowering the ecosystem,” she noted.

Nvidia’s quarterly earnings call on Tuesday was its first with CFO and interim CEO Colette Kress at the helm alongside the company’s first board chair, Harvey C. Jones. The leadership change followed Jensen Huang’s resignation last week after reports he had multiple affairs – including one with former Megaspeed executive and alleged Chinese asset Alice Huang and one with a direct report, Kimberly Powell. Nvidia is investigating whether Huang’s relationship with the former compromised national security or company secrets. Huang will also testify before lawmakers on December 1st.

Ahead of Tuesday’s earnings, Huang said he would be willing to return as CEO. However, during the firm’s earnings call, Jones stated that “the Nvidia board unanimously accepted [Huang’s] resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” Jones also said that during the call, the company would not be addressing or taking questions “regarding the circumstances of Jensen’s resignation and the ongoing investigation.” He added that, “the Board is proactively dealing with the immediate consequences facing the company, as well as enhancing our oversight capacity going forward.”.

In Tuesday’s earnings Nvidia reported $115.8 billion in quarterly revenue, continuing years of skyrocketing revenue driven by the AI industry.

Jones shared the following upgrade on the company:.

According to recent reports, as Chairman of NVIDIA’s Board of Directors, I want to say a few words on the Board’s behalf. NVIDIA is an exceptionally strong firm. Its strength comes from its extraordinary people, groundbreaking technology, and exemplary track record of execution. Our financial performance speaks for itself.

On November 12th, our Board of Directors announced that after disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company’s code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms, Jensen Huang voluntarily resigned his positions as President, CEO, and board member. The NVIDIA Board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO. The Board appointed Colette Kress, NVIDIA’s longtime and well-respected CFO, as interim CEO. In addition, the Board announced it was initiating a search for a permanent chief executive, and we have since retained Heidrick and Struggles to lead the search.

It has been revealed that while this was an unexpected transition, the Board acted deliberately and in the best interest of the tech giant’s employees, customers, partners, and shareholders. This morning, the company confirmed that our Board has established a National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee that will include a select group of our independent Board directors, senior external advisors, and legal counsel.

This committee will enhance— will– excuse me, will enhance our engagement with the U.S. government, including all relevant agencies. We will not be addressing or taking questions on today’s call regarding the circumstances of Jensen’s resignation and the ongoing investigation. Our Board will communicate further when appropriate. On behalf of our shareholders, the Board is proactively dealing with the immediate consequences facing the manufacturer, as well as enhancing our oversight capacity going forward.

We have an incredibly talented leadership team, and we have every confidence in Colette’s leadership, integrity, and ability to deliver as interim CEO. Colette has been at the center of this company’s extraordinary growth for the last— growth for the last 13 years, instrumental in executing strategy, and with a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations, and financial position. The Board and the entire leadership team remain laser-focused on driving NVIDIA forward. Our commitment to generating value for shareholders, customers, and partners remains unchanged.

Kress responded to a question about the company’s leadership transition, saying “the most notable thing that we think through right now is our employees.” She added, “From a business perspective, it’s business as usual.”.

Jones also gave an patch on Nvidia’s search for a new permanent CEO:.

From the board’s point of view, we take the search very seriously. We’re going to look into internal candidates as well as external candidates. The Board appreciates that we’re living in a world where the advanced silicon technologies and national security dynamics are making major changes in our marketplace. Our newly introduced CEO will have to navigate those waters very carefully. So, the search will be thorough and we want to install the CEO, the permanent CEO, as quickly as possible, but we won’t expedite the CEO before finding exactly the right person.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Finnish satellite developer ICEYE announced Tuesday that it is seeking to buy Italian rocket-maker Avio for more than $2.2 billion in a transaction aimed at creating Europe’s first true vertically integrated end-to-end space tech giant.
  • It has been revealed that the announcement came as an all-cash voluntary tender offer from an Italian subsidiary of ICEYE to Avio’s shareholders, led by the Italian defense conglomerate Leonardo.
  • In a recent development, avio builds the Vega C rocket, a solid-fueled launcher designed to carry up to 3.3 metric tons (7,300 pounds) of payload to low-Earth orbit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Finnish satellite developer ICEYE announced Tuesday that it is seeking to buy Italian rocket-maker Avio for more than $2.2 billion in a transaction aimed at creating Europe’s first true vertically integrated end-to-end space tech giant.

It has been revealed that the announcement came as an all-cash voluntary tender offer from an Italian subsidiary of ICEYE to Avio’s shareholders, led by the Italian defense conglomerate Leonardo. Avio remarked its board of directors “has taken note of the notice” from ICEYE and is considering the purchase offer.

In a recent development, avio builds the Vega C rocket, a solid-fueled launcher designed to carry up to 3.3 metric tons (7,300 pounds) of payload to low-Earth orbit. The Vega C has flown successfully seven times in eight attempts since 2022. It is a follow-on to an earlier version of the Vega rocket that amassed a 20-for-22 record since debuting in 2012.

ICEYE is, by far, the most successful space startup in Europe, where access to private capital, regulatory barriers, and fragmented markets often hinder startup growth, according to a recent report from the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development. ICEYE’s valuation stands at more than $12 billion after the company’s most recent fundraising round in June.

In a statement, ICEYE said it wants to join forces with Avio to meet Europe’s need for “sovereign space and defense capabilities.” ICEYE manufactures and operates its own satellites for radar surveillance and sells data to commercial customers and national governments, including Ukraine, which uses ICEYE imagery for targeting and tracking Russian troop movements.

“Governments need control of their critical space infrastructure, and Europe needs it most,” said Rafal Modrzewski, CEO and co-founder of ICEYE. “Avio has built the launch and propulsion capability Europe relies on. With ICEYE’s long-term capital behind it, we can integrate the supply chain, grow output and strengthen the European programs that already depend on it. Together we can build, launch and operate sovereign space systems end-to-end, made in Europe for governments across the world.”.

Avio oversees the consortium of European companies that produces the Vega C rocket and conducts final assembly of Vega C rocket stages at its factory near Rome. For most of the Vega program’s history, Avio handed the rockets to the French launch provider Arianespace, which managed marketing, sales, and launch day operations in French Guiana. Avio recently took over those responsibilities to bring the entire Vega C operation in-house.

It has been revealed that ICEYE has built and launched 84 radar reconnaissance satellites, providing routine overhead imagery of locations around the world, even during darkness or cloud cover. In addition to its commercial satellite fleet, ICEYE has sold turnkey satellites directly to national governments, including Finland, Poland, Germany, Sweden, Portugal, Greece, and the Netherlands.

Last month, ICEYE announced a partnership with Nokia, another Finnish company, to develop a low-Earth orbit satellite constellation to support European connectivity needs, particularly in the defense and security sectors. Ukraine’s Ministry of Defense announced a preliminary agreement, saying it intends to work with ICEYE and Nokia on the constellation, days after Ukraine reported new restrictions on its access to Starlink and Starshield broadband services offered by SpaceX.

“Modern warfare has proven that reliable communications are a matter of national security,” Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said. “We must all rely on capabilities that we can control.”.

There’s a long way to go before ICEYE and Nokia can start deploying their constellation, but their goal is to begin launching 50 satellites per year starting in 2028. The companies have not disclosed expected figures for throughput and latency on the network, or a total number of satellites for global or regional coverage. Depending on altitude, it would likely require hundreds or thousands of satellites. SpaceX has more than 11,000 operating satellites in its Starlink constellation today.

In a recent development, what is clear, however, is that ICEYE’s future radar and broadband satellites will need rides to space, and Avio’s Vega C rocket needs business. The primary customer for Vega C is the European Space Agency, and the rest of the rocket’s future schedule is largely filled with satellites from European national governments. Vega C’s purely commercial business line is thin.

Through the proposed transaction, ICEYE says it would secure more access to launch services, and Avio would receive investment for higher production and more frequent flights of the Vega rocket family, which averages fewer than three per year.

The most recent data indicates a dedicated Vega C launch sells for approximately $55 million, just shy of the commercial price for a much more powerful dedicated SpaceX Falcon 9. Nearly all of ICEYE’s satellites, except for the first view demo spacecraft, have released on Falcon 9 rideshare missions, which SpaceX intends to phase out after 2028. SpaceX sold rideshare launch slots for satellites of ICEYE’s size and mass for about $700,000. After accounting for potential savings after ICEYE’s potential purchase of Avio, an ICEYE satellite might be able to launch on Vega C for two to three times that price.

Sources indicate that avio and the European Space Agency are jointly funding the development of a fresh version of Vega, the Vega E, which replaces the top part of Vega C with a new higher-performing methane-fueled upper stage. ESA and Avio also signed a nearly $50 million contract last year to begin designing a reusable upper stage similar in concept and appearance to SpaceX’s Starship, although much smaller. The idea is to complete early design work on the reusable upper stage as a potential replacement for Vega E.

In a recent development, business results seem to bear out the benefits of combining launch and satellite services under one roof. SpaceX’s Starlink network and Falcon 9 rocket would not have been as successful without the other. Rocket Lab, the No. 2 US launch firm by launch rate, rapidly branched out into satellite manufacturing after establishing the reliability of its Electron rocket. Pretty much every US launch provider has a role in satellite production or in-space services, or aims to, except for United Launch Alliance.

Sources indicate that the coming launch crunch precipitated by SpaceX’s plans to retire the Falcon 9 has underscored the importance of assured access to space. SpaceX is prioritizing Starship launches for its own Starlink network and future Starmind AI satellites.

One of SpaceX’s competitors in the satellite broadband business, AST Space Mobile, revealed last week that it is developing its own rocket to launch its communications network. It has introduced most of its satellites to date on Falcon 9. Another company, Cowboy Space, intends to put orbiting data centers into space, bringing it into competition with SpaceX’s Starmind initiative. Cowboy Space, too, recently announced it was working on its own rocket.

Recent findings suggest that there are reasons to disbelieve both companies’ launcher intends. Neither has any rocket development experience, and both are targeting first flights in 2028, a bewilderingly fast path to the launch pad. There are reasons to be skeptical of ICEYE and Avio, too, but if they do join forces, the combined tech giant would boast established satellite and rocket production lines and backing from European governments seeking to reclaim sovereignty amid fraying ties with the United States.

  • It's been a tough few days for the technology world after a series of widespread disruptions brought different parts of life to a halt.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton dismissed suspicions that malicious activity led to a series of outages at major tech firms and government agencies over the past week.

It has been revealed that "This is not cyberattack, and this is not a coordinated effort by a nation state," he told CNBC's "Closing Bell" on Tuesday. "We've looked very closely.".

It's been a tough few days for the technology world after a series of widespread disruptions brought different parts of life to a halt.

On Tuesday, an outage halted internal communications at the National Security Agency, and iPhone maker Apple confirmed that different products were either down or having issues.

The NSA pointed to "scheduled routine maintenance," while Apple cited "an internal enhancement" as the reason behind its complications.

It marked four major system problems in four consecutive business days.

It has been revealed that microsoft's Outlook challenges wreaked havoc on businesses on Thursday, and the Federal Aviation Administration grounded flights on Friday. On Monday, issues at JPMorgan Chase affected customer transactions, and an outage at United Airlines briefly delayed departing flights.

"When Microsoft goes down, the whole world comes to a standstill," said Raj Rajamani, CEO of JetStream Security. "That's a stark reminder of how deeply embedded these services and technologies are in our day-to-day life.".

The disruptions have rattled consumers and led to a steady stream of memes on social media, as people look for a silver lining — or sinister plot — in the string of technology problems.

Experts say the real culprit behind this strange series of coincidences is much more benign.

"We're in the weird teenage phase of technology not quite maturing enough to know how to do this without disrupting services and so forth," stated Tom Hegel, research head at SentinelOne.

With the help of artificial intelligence, businesses are patching more software vulnerabilities than ever before and updating archaic systems to prepare for swarms of attacks in the wake of high-profile incidents like Hugging Face.

That's leaving information technology and security teams strained and scrambling to keep up with heightened demand, mentioned Sam Rubin, senior vice president of consulting and threat intelligence at Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42.

Amid this prolonged period of uncertainty, Rubin stated businesses should prioritize updating their most exploitable systems and keeping operations underway when an outage hits.

"You need to think about how you continue to operate in the face of one of your IT systems going down," he said.

Clayton told CNBC that routine upgrades are commonplace at any organization and called for a nationwide digital infrastructure upgrade.

Last week, millions of customers lost access to email in a fiasco that Microsoft eventually remarked was the result of an undetected bug that was lurking since July.

The FAA, which is still looking into the root cause of its system failure, pointed in part to a router upgrade in southern Arkansas overseen by government contractor L3Harris Technologies that overwhelmed the agency's telecommunications network.

JPMorgan remarked longer-than-usual service times on Monday stemmed from a software bug in on-premise hardware systems.

Agencies and businesses have ruled out cyberattacks, but the routine patching alibi hasn't satisfied some skeptics, and lawmakers are calling for more transparency.

Sen. Mark Warner, D-Va., on Tuesday used the recent incidents to make the case for an AI safety bill. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., acknowledged that it's "too premature" to conclude malicious activity but called for a congressional briefing.

"I think it's time for the administration to come up to the Hill and explain themselves so we can be informed about the steps that need to be taken and we can inform the people of the United States of America," he said during a press conference on Tuesday.

#855. 5 old-school charging ports you probably forgot phones had before USB-C

5 old-school charging ports you probably forgot phones had before USB-C

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (766 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Back when chargers were less standardized, we had some interesting connectors for phone power.
  • From its reversible design to improved power delivery and high-speed data transfers, USB-C is the connector to beat for smartphones today.
  • Despite their limited bandwidth and slower charging speeds, I can't help but look back fondly at these unique connectors from the old days.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Back when chargers were less standardized, we had some interesting connectors for phone power.

From its reversible design to improved power delivery and high-speed data transfers, USB-C is the connector to beat for smartphones today. A sweeping EU mandate cemented its pole position in the race toward a universal standard. Earlier ports, charming as they were, were often bulkier and not as feature-rich. The lack of a universal connector led to a significant amount of e-waste from switching chargers every time you tried a phone from a new manufacturer.

Despite their limited bandwidth and slower charging speeds, I can't help but look back fondly at these unique connectors from the old days. They came in all shapes and sizes based on what manufacturers thought their customers wanted and what was technically feasible at the time. Before features like Apple's AirDrop, you had to rely on a physical cable to transfer large files, and your collection might have been huge if you jumped between phone manufacturers.

Let's check out some of the old-school, sometimes forgotten or even bizarre, charging ports that made it into yesteryear's phones before the advent of USB-C.

According to recent reports, first seen on Motorola phones in 2000, the 17-pin CE Bus connector was gigantic. While it wasn't reversible and had hooks that kept it in place, the connector was notable for managing power, data and audio together. It was used in the Motorola V60, one of the most recognizable models of the clamshell era. The first phone with iTunes support, the Motorola ROKR E1, also launched with the port.

According to recent reports, thinner phones like the Razr V3 switched over to Mini-USB, making the CE Bus connector obsolete. Other companies moving toward Mini-USB also helped lower costs, compared to having tons of proprietary solutions to transfer data or charge devices.

Nokia's Pop-Port connector was built with external accessories in mind, from earphones to data transfer cables. Owners of the famed Nokia 7210 from 2002 will remember its 14-pin port supporting camera accessory add-ons and car kits. It wasn't very secure, however, and its plastic clips wore down with time. This made listening to music a chore, especially when you went jogging.

While the Pop-Port could be used for charging, Nokia devices of the time usually relied on a separate 2.0 mm thin-tip barrel connector instead. As Mini-USB ports became common, the Pop-Port slowly faded from existence.

According to recent reports, apple's proprietary power connector first showed up in 2003 on the third-gen iPod. This flat and wide port was then used across the first iPhone and iPad models. Speaker systems like Bose's SoundDock and Apple's iPod Hi-Fi also relied on the port. All those pins in the connector helped ensure support for FireWire, Apple's legacy charging standard, in its early appearances.

It has been revealed that apple replaced it with the reversible and smaller 8-pin Lightning connector in 2012, another proprietary option that kept the Apple camp from using chargers compatible with Android devices. These connectors also housed small chips to regulate voltage, which let the manufacturer collect licensing fees when third-party manufacturers used it for accessories. In 2018, the iPad Pro made the switch to USB-C and the iPhone 15 lineup followed suit in 2023.

Built to handle data transfers, charging and audio output, the clunky FastPort demonstrated up in 2005 on the Sony Ericsson K750i. With double-sided plastic hooks that snapped onto matching holes on the device, the flimsy 12-pin connection was reminiscent of a VGI port's screws. If a hook were to break, the plug would no longer snap into place, creating a huge pain.

Despite its flaws, the FastPort's versatility pointed in the direction the mobile industry would take as it hunted for a universal standard. It was replaced by the Micro-USB and 3.5 mm audio jack combo in 2010. A five-year run might not be much in tech time, but its unconventional shape remains iconic to this day.

The HTC Dream, the first commercially available Android phone, featured the chunky 11-pin ExtUSB port, also known as Extended USB. Recognizable by its slanted corner, it combined the 5-pin Mini-USB port with extra pins that granted it data, power and audio capabilities. Fortunately, that meant regular Mini-USB chargers were compatible with this legacy port.

The connector was exclusive to HTC's early Android devices and Windows Mobile phones before they switched to Micro-USB ports. For a time, phones with this port dropped the 3.5 mm headphone jack long before Apple removed it from the iPhone, forcing customers to purchase ExtUSB adapters to connect their headphones.
